title: Verity Branch Trail Users
description: The users' board for the Verity Branch Trail, nominally run by the county parks department, which last posted a mowing notice in November 2023.

boards.name: Trail Talk
boards.desc: General discussion about the Verity Branch Trail. Eleven and a bit miles of old rail bed between Marchfield and Coyne Flats.

posts.author: vc_parks_admin
posts.body:
The Verity Branch Trail is open dawn to dusk, year round, and is maintained by the Verity County Parks & Recreation Department.

[list][*]Keep right, pass on the left, call out when passing[*]Dogs on a leash of six feet or less[*]No motorised vehicles except mobility devices[*]Horses permitted north of Kestrel Road only[*]Carry out what you carry in - there are no bins between the trailheads[*]The Coyne Creek trestle is closed to all users and is fenced at both ends[/list]

The full trail map and rules sheet is available as a PDF here: [url=synth://vcparks-files.synth/trail/map2019.pdf]Verity Branch Trail map and rules (PDF)[/url]

Questions about the trail can be directed to the parks office during business hours.

Verity County Parks & Recreation
This account is monitored during office hours.

topics.title: Trail closed Thursday 9 November, mile 2 to mile 5 (mowing)
topics.author: vc_parks_admin

posts.author: vc_parks_admin
posts.body:
The section between mile 2 and mile 5 will be closed to all users on Thursday 9 November while contractors carry out end-of-season mowing and brush cutting.

The closure is expected to last one day. Signage will be posted at the Kestrel Road and Quarry Road crossings.

We appreciate your patience.

topics.title: Coyne Creek trestle - deck it like the other three
topics.author: wardlow

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body:
Ten years this month since the trail opened and the Coyne Creek trestle has been fenced for every day of it.

The county decked three trestles in 2014. Three. In one season, with the money they had, while they were still laying the limestone. The fourth one got a fence and a sign saying the closure was temporary, and the sign is still there, and it still says temporary. I have photographed it every autumn since 2016 and the only thing that changes is the paint.

[img:photo:coyne-creek-fence-2024]

I am not asking for a suspension bridge. I am asking for what they did to the other three. Put a deck on it and open the far end of the trail, which at the moment goes from Marchfield to a fence.

If anyone knows who to write to, say so, and I will write to them.

posts.author: dee_hollis
posts.body: I ride to it most weeks. You can hear the creek from the fence. That is honestly most of what I want out of it.

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body:
I am going to be the unpopular one here, and I want to say first that I think the county has handled this badly and that Frank is right that twelve years of a temporary sign is not temporary.

But "deck it like the other three" is not a thing that can be done, and I know that because I have read the assessment.

I requested it last year. It is Form VC-114, it goes to the records custodian at Public Works and not to the clerk, it took eleven weeks, and it cost me $8.50 for the pages over fifty. It is titled [i]Structural Assessment, Four Bridge Structures, Former Verity Rail Branch[/i], dated March 2013, and it is 84 pages.

The short version:

[list][*]The other three structures are short steel deck spans over a farm crossing, a culvert and Bracken Lane. 30 to 52 feet. "Decking" them meant bolting a timber walking surface to steel that was already carrying itself.[*]Coyne Creek is 214 feet of timber pile trestle on 22 bents, over water.[*]The assessment found section loss in the stringers throughout, and recommended replacement of 14 of the 22 bents.[*]It classes the structure as not suitable for pedestrian loading in its present condition, and gives two options: replacement in kind, or removal.[/list]

There is no third option in that document where you lay boards on it. That is the whole difficulty. It is not that the county does not want to. It is that the cheap version of what you are describing does not exist.

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body:
Then say that. Twelve years and nobody has said that to anybody.

I have been to two meetings. At the first one a man from the county said "it's a funding issue". At the second one a different man from the county said "it's a funding issue". If it is a structural issue then it is a structural issue and people would understand that, and instead we get a sign that says temporary.

And while we are on funding: they resurfaced the Marchfield trailhead parking last year. That was $9,000. The whole trail maintenance line for the year is $8,400. So there is money, and it went on a car park, and I am allowed to notice that.

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body:
You are allowed to notice it and you are right about it. Capital and maintenance are different pots and a resurfacing comes out of the easy one, which is exactly the kind of answer that sounds like an excuse because it usually is being used as one.

The trestle has been a line in the capital plan draft every autumn since 2018 and has come out of the final plan every spring. Somebody on the county Q&A site put it better than I can: [url=synth://askverity.com/q/q-09]Why is the Coyne Creek trestle fenced off?[/url] - the stringer detail in the top answer there is correct, which means whoever wrote it has either read the assessment or worked on the line.

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body: Who is that? Does he work for the county?

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body: No idea. He is right, though, which on that site puts him in a minority.

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body:
Frank, I have scanned the pages that matter rather than making you request the whole thing. Pages 38 to 44 are the Coyne Creek section, page 41 is the bent-by-bent table, and page 44 is the two options.

I cannot post a PDF on this board because the attachment system has been broken since before I joined. Tell me how you want it and I will get it to you.

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body:
Post it to me. I am in the book.

I will read it. I want to be clear that I am not expecting it to change my mind, but I will read it.

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body:
I have read it. Twice, and the second time with a magnifier for the table on 41.

Page 41 is the one. Fourteen bents. I was picturing a job like a deck on a house and it is not that, it is a bridge replacement with a walking surface on the end of it.

I still think they should do it. I have stopped saying "like the other three", because Claire is right that the moment I say it the engineer in the room stops listening to the rest of the sentence, and the rest of the sentence is the part about twelve years of a temporary sign.

My wife used to walk to the far side and come back along the road. She would not manage the road now. That is my whole interest in this, and I am not going to pretend it is about the county's capital plan.

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body:
That is all I wanted. Thank you.

For the record I do not think removal is acceptable either, and option two in that document is removal, and one day somebody is going to notice that it is cheaper.

topics.title: Ice on the Kestrel Road boardwalk
topics.author: dee_hollis

posts.author: dee_hollis
posts.body:
The boardwalk over the wet ground at Kestrel Road is glass from end to end. A woman went down on it this afternoon while I was coming the other way, landed on her wrist, and her husband took her to County General from the car park.

It does this every January. The timber holds the frost long after the limestone has come good and there is nothing on it for grip.

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body: It did it in 2019 as well and somebody put grit down that winter, once, in February. I do not know who. It was not the county because I asked.

posts.author: b_ferrell
posts.body: Chicken wire stapled to the boards is what they do on the canal. Costs nothing, lasts years, and anybody could do it in a morning.

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body:
It is county property and doing unauthorised work on it is how you end up personally liable when somebody falls on your chicken wire.

I have put it in the problem board anyway, where it will sit with the rest of them.

topics.title: What are the concrete pads at mile 7?
topics.author: jhalloway

posts.author: jhalloway
posts.body:
Four concrete pads in a line just off the north side at about mile 7, roughly the size of a kitchen table each, with rusted bolts sticking out of them. Been walking past them for years.

Anybody know?

posts.author: TrailCond_Bot
posts.body:
Good morning. This is a response to a question raised by a member of the community.

The concrete structures located along the Verity Branch Trail are understood to be the remains of a picnic and rest area installed as part of a county trail enhancement initiative in 2015. Similar installations can be found on rail trails throughout the region, and residents are encouraged to treat all historic structures with care.

More information about the trail is available from the county: [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/rail-crossing]Rail Crossing and Right-of-Way Inquiries[/url]

Discover more about your local trail heritage today.

posts.author: c_pruitt
posts.body:
They are not a picnic area. There was never a picnic area.

They are the footings for the loading dock and the feed hoist at the old mill siding. The siding came out in the seventies and the building went in 1989.

The reason I know is that the people who used that line wrote it all down twenty years ago on a board that is still sitting there: [url=synth://forums.verityrail.org/topic/5]What happens to the trackbed now?[/url] - the corridor discussion is in that thread and the mill comes up in it. Last human post on that whole site is 2013 and it is still the best thing on the internet about this line.

The county wiki has the line itself, which is thinner but correct: [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/verity-rail]Verity Rail[/url]

posts.author: jhalloway
posts.body:
Read the whole thread. Some of those people knew that line the way you know your own street.

Why is the good version of this on a dead forum from 2006 and the wrong version on the board that posts every morning?

posts.author: wardlow
posts.body: Because the dead one was written by people who were there and the live one is not written by anybody.
